Hi Aria / Ben,

Adding some legal context from the TIA perspective. I am attaching a short TIA summary (TIA_summary.docx) with findings — highlights below.

- Legal framing: Hashing / truncation lowers identifiability but does not automatically remove the need for transfer safeguards. Both the EU SCCs and the UK Addendum require a TIA where transfers involve jurisdictions with differing adequacy. Pseudonymisation is a risk mitigation factor in the TIA, but technical/organizational controls still matter.

- Controls we rely on and can represent in the DPA annex:
  * Region pinning with strong routing rules (no egress from pinned region for inference logs)
  * Encryption at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.2+), with customer-managed keys available for Private deployments
  * KV cache lifecycle: ephemeral in-memory KV caches on GPUs are zeroed on instance termination; persistent dumps are disabled for Dedicated/Private unless explicitly enabled by customer for debugging
  * Logging minimisation: retention windows configurable by customer; default retention for debug logs is 7 days and aggregated usage metrics are rolled up and stripped of identifiers before export
  * Subprocessor constraints: subprocessors that access raw inference logs are engaged only in EU regions for customers who require EU-only processing; analytics subprocessors handle aggregated, pseudonymised counts and are contractually prohibited from attempting re-identification

- Recommendation on SCCs/UK Addendum: Attach the EU SCCs for transfers out of the EEA. For transfers to the UK, add the UK Addendum to the SCCs. Where appropriate we can include an annex stating that for region-pinned Dedicated/Private deployments Redwood will not initiate transfers out of the pinned region absent written instruction.

I attached a compact TIA_summary.docx (3 pages) and drafted a short clause we can put in the DPA (I will circulate a plain-text draft if you want). Let me know if GlobeTrotter would prefer a longer TIA or a technical appendix for your security team.

Cheers,

Aria — appreciate the detailed follow ups. Answers below and next steps attached.

1) KV cache / crash-dumps: Confirmed — we do not persist GPU KV cache snapshots to cross-region object storage as part of normal operations. Crash-dump capture is possible but is disabled by default and requires explicit opt-in by the customer. When enabled, engineers may pull a dump into a secure bucket in the same region for triage; cross-region export requires a formal change request and customer sign-off.

2) Analytics subprocessor feeds: The US analytics vendor receives aggregated telemetry only: event counts, anonymised model identifiers (hashed), sampling rate, and aggregated latency buckets. They do not receive raw prompts, un-hashed user IDs, or full inference logs. Contractually, subprocessors are prohibited from attempting re-identification and are bound by our DPA flow-down clauses and SOC2 obligations; see subprocessor_map_v2.csv for named vendors and country locations.

3) Draft contractual sentence (Redwood-approved):

"For any Customer electing region‑pinned EU processing under this Agreement, Redwood shall not transfer, nor permit the transfer of, inference logs or raw inference artifacts outside the European Economic Area, except upon Customer's prior written instruction or where required by applicable law; such transfers will be subject to appropriate transfer safeguards (e.g., EU SCCs and any applicable UK Addendum)."

I've attached a short text file with that clause (dpa-clause-draft.txt) and a more detailed subprocessor-delegation-log.csv. We've also put these materials in a shared Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Gx-Redwood-GlobeTrotter-DPA.

- If your team would like a longer TIA we can expand the TIA_summary into a 7–10 page appendix with logs/retention examples.
